solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Tiger, say, having a fit of bad temper — he's a disaster!

parts.note: a tiger is an example of a cat, the 'say' signalling an example
a strop is a sulky fit of bad temper
he, taken as written, with the 's as a linking 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a man in a tigerish temper tantrum as a walking calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiger, say' looks like a description of the man, but it just stands for the family it belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a sudden great calamity, the same as a disaster.

clue.text: Record area — oddly rich source of honey

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word rich

parts.note: a hive is where bees make honey

explanation.surface: A note about an area that is unusually rich in honey production.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored record or collection of documents, so the noun senses match.

clue.text: A time to give? Now!

parts.note: to present is to give something formally, as a gift

explanation.surface: A question about the right moment for gift-giving, answered with an urgent 'Now!'.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark reads like a query about timing, but the first half is pure wordplay and 'Now!' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at this moment, in the current time.

clue.text: More or less below belt, ultimately? No, above it

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means this piece follows the other in the answer
ultimately points to the final letter of the word belt

parts.note: the phrase 'or so' means more or less, approximately

explanation.surface: Someone guesses something sits roughly below the belt, then corrects themselves: no, it is above.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the body's trunk is not below the belt but above it, so 'No, above it' corrects the wordplay's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body sits above the waist and belt line, correcting the 'below' of the wordplay.

clue.text: Organising revolt, why broadcast in public?

indicators.note: organising suggests arranging these letters into a new order
broadcast means spoken out over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the word why is said aloud and heard as the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone planning a rebellion wonders why it should be announced openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organising' rearranges REVOLT into OVERTL; 'broadcast' turns WHY into its sound-alike letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means openly, done where everyone can see, which is acting in public.

clue.text: Harry? Bound to get out!

parts.note: the famous escapologist Harry, tied up in chains and certain to free himself

explanation.surface: Someone named Harry is sure to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'certain', but it also means tied up, which is how the famous escapologist always began.
explanation.definitionFit: The escape artist Harry was famous for freeing himself from chains, ropes and locked boxes.

clue.text: In the jet set, maybe, with second one of four children in police force

parts.note: members of the jet set are often in the air, travelling by plane
a quad, short for quadruplet, is one of four children born together

explanation.surface: A jet-setter with a quadruplet sibling ends up in the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The FLYING SQUAD is a London Metropolitan Police unit dealing with serious armed crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flying Squad is a specialist British police unit, so it is a branch of the force.

clue.text: Article left in Indian state or country

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast

explanation.surface: A piece of writing left behind in an Indian state or some other country.
explanation.definitionFit: Angola is a nation in south-western Africa.

clue.text: What may stop you shooting in exotic places around pole

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the word places is rearranged

parts.note: N, for north, is one of the magnetic poles

explanation.surface: Something that might halt a photographer in faraway locations near a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns, but it means photography. 'Exotic' turns PLACES into LESCAP, and 'around' wraps it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens cap covers a camera lens, so while it is on you cannot take pictures.

clue.text: Runs home, disheartened with South American primate

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle, the heart, of the word home is removed

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Someone runs home, dejected, alongside a monkey from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as describing the primate, but it splits into S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey, and monkeys are primates.

clue.text: Pioneers in heavy metal and rock covering article

parts.note: lead is a heavy metallic element

indicators.note: covering means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to rock is to sway from side to side
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Trailblazers in heavy metal and rock music cover an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal and rock' reads as music genres, but they are lead and sway.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pioneers goes first and shows others the route, which is to lead the way.

clue.text: Praise new ideologies dismissing ego

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of ideologies are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: ego is taken as written, its letters removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone acclaims fresh belief systems that leave out self-importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' is part of the composite anagram signal: after the removal, 'new' rearranges the leftover letters IDOLIS... into the answer, so 'ideologies' never appears intact.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to worship or admire them greatly, a strong form of praising them.

clue.text: Brief description of unfashionable occupation

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a line, as in line of work, is an occupation

explanation.surface: A short account of a job that is out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a summary giving the main features, a short description.

clue.text: Look around back of hall and put a film on

indicators.note: around means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: back of points to the last letter of the word hall

explanation.surface: Someone glances round the back of a hall and then screens a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put a film on' suggests showing a movie, but it means coating with a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: To glaze is to coat something with a thin shiny layer, as on pottery or pastry.

clue.text: Prison sentence given to precocious chorus singer?

indicators.note: given to means this piece is attached to the other, which comes after it

parts.note: precocious means developing early
bird is slang for a prison term, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time

explanation.surface: A gifted young choir member is handed a jail term.
explanation.walkthrough: The dawn chorus is birdsong at first light, so an early bird is one of its singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds singing at dawn form the dawn chorus, so an early riser among birds sings in it.

clue.text: Obscene ruling covering half of pubs

indicators.note: covering means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of pubs

explanation.surface: A ruling that extends over half the pubs is considered indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruling' looks like a noun meaning a decision, but it is the adjective REGNANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means deeply offensive or disgusting, close to obscene.

clue.text: Measure applied to sensitive area in dance

indicators.note: applied to means this piece is attached after the other one

parts.note: the quick is the tender flesh under a fingernail
a step is a measure taken to achieve something

explanation.surface: A treatment is put on a tender spot during a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The quickstep is a fast ballroom dance.

clue.text: One married type's distinctive influence

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
print means printed type, the 's linking as 'is'

explanation.surface: A married individual's personality leaves a particular mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a lasting mark or effect someone leaves, a characteristic influence.

clue.text: Cutting jack leaves hazard for articulated lorry

indicators.note: leaves means the word jack departs, removed from the longer word

parts.note: jackknifing is when a lorry's trailer swings round against its cab
jack is taken as written

explanation.surface: A slashing incident where a jack falls off, endangering a big truck.
explanation.walkthrough: An articulated lorry is a tractor unit pulling a trailer, called a semi or tractor-trailer in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Knifing is stabbing or slashing with a blade, a form of cutting.

clue.text: One who's left the country as a result of Old Father Time

parts.note: ex means former, so old
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone emigrates because of the march of Father Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Father Time' looks like one personification, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat, short for expatriate, lives outside their native land.

clue.text: Palestine ordered to release an apostle's letter

indicators.note: ordered signals that the letters of Palestine are rearranged into a new sequence

parts.note: an is taken as written, its letters removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Palestine is told to free a written message from one of Christ's followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to release' is part of the composite anagram signal: after the removal, 'ordered' rearranges the seven remaining letters, and 'apostle's' tells you which kind of letter is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament epistles are letters written by apostles such as Paul.

clue.text: Flat areas east of Israel surrounded by troubles

indicators.note: surrounded by means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: pains are troubles or efforts

indicators.note: east of points to the rightmost, final letter of the word Israel

explanation.surface: Level lands lying east of Israel are beset by conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east of Israel' reads as geography, but on a map east is right, so it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plains are wide expanses of level land.

clue.text: Fill post — a quiet position in field

parts.note: p, for piano, means quietly in music
point is a cricket fielding position, square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A job is filled with a calm cricket fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to assign them to a job, which fills that post.

clue.text: Army volunteers set off to get experience

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong, so the word set is jumbled

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers head out to gain some practical knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' reads as 'departed', but 'off' rearranges SET into STE.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to experience it briefly, as in a taste of freedom.

clue.text: Expression of sorrow mainly enveloping Scotsman

indicators.note: enveloping means the first piece wraps around the second
mainly means most of the word, dropping the last letter

parts.note: grief is deep sorrow
Mac is an informal name for a Scotsman, from the prefix in many Scottish surnames

explanation.surface: A face of sadness wrapped around a Scottish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expression of sorrow' looks like the definition, but 'of sorrow' is wordplay: 'mainly' cuts GRIEF to GRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of pain or disgust.

clue.text: Mischief-makers from team tucking into pastries

indicators.note: tucking into means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: pies are pastry dishes
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Troublemakers from a sports squad wolf down cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' reads as eating, but it means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixies are mischievous fairies in folklore.

clue.text: Broadcaster exposed by comedian ten named

indicators.note: exposed by means the letters are revealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is unmasked by a comedian who names ten.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an aerial, which transmits or picks up radio signals.

clue.text: Party worker lets out insects

parts.note: a stag party is a groom's pre-wedding night out
a worker bee is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the word lets is rearranged

explanation.surface: A party staff member releases bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lets out' reads as releases, but 'out' rearranges LETS into TLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag beetles are large beetles with antler-like jaws, and beetles are insects.
